q: The maximum entropy principle (MaxEnt, Jaynes 1957) states that the best probability distribution for an inference problem is the one that:
opts: Maximises the Shannon entropy subject to the constraints (known moment conditions, given information)
Minimises KL divergence from a flat prior
exp: Jaynes' MaxEnt: given constraints ⟨fᵢ(X)⟩ = aᵢ, the maximum entropy distribution is the Gibbs distribution P ∝ exp(Σ λᵢfᵢ(x)) (Lagrange multipliers). This is the least informative (least biased) distribution consistent with the known constraints, and is the unique maximum of H(P).
